claim: High-NA EUV adoption is split: Intel runs specific Intel 18A layers on High-NA in volume production and plans it for 14A (which it says it may pause without an external customer), SK hynix has a production tool for DRAM and Samsung is reported to have bought two for 2nm foundry and DRAM, while TSMC owns High-NA tools for R&D but keeps them out of production on cost grounds through at least A14. So High-NA demand in 2026-2028 comes from Intel (18A layers now, 14A later) and the two Korean memory makers, not mainly from Intel 14A.
notes: Interpretation of CLM-1707 (Intel 18A HVM on High-NA), CLM-1709 (14A pause risk), CLM-1710 (SK hynix), CLM-1713 (Samsung, press report), CLM-1714 and CLM-1715 (TSMC). Drops CLM-1747's 'with multi-patterning', which TSMC declined to confirm (Tom's Hardware, SRC-0586).
